proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an original fixed-n exact-uniform sparse-nuisance converse, including the n^(-2/7) stress-tuple lower bound, and derived a sufficient polynomial separation between unknown- and known-propensity experiments. Two distinct attaining-test architectures—pair-factor and projected full-cell kernels—failed explicit population-signal kill tests after bounded repairs. A matching sparse upper bound, dense-regime nuisance converse, transition logarithms, and the necessary-and-sufficient propensity frontier remain open.
tldr: Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  The observational radius satisfies the proved all-regime upper bound \(\rho_n^*\le Cb_n\) and, for \(d\ge2s_0\), the original fixed-sample lower bound \(\rho_n^*\ge c\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\}\), with no logarithm at \(d=2s_0\).  The no-penalty region \(s_0\ge\gamma\), \(d\le4\gamma\) remains matched.  A strict penalty is now proved whenever \(\gamma>s_0\) and \(d>2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\): then \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\ge c n^{2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\to\infty\).  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the exponent is at least \(4/35\).  The complete frontier and its remaining transition boundaries are open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.
gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures establish asymptotic validity or power under structured directions and nuisance learner conditions; published minimax results instead treat pointwise CATE estimation, conditional independence under different geometry, signed expected covariance, or heteroskedasticity. None gives the fixed-sample critical radius over the identical binary causal class with three separate Hölder indices and an unknown constant null.
fill: The analysis starts from an exact binned covariance identity, profiles the unknown constant inside a fourth-order statistic, exposes every bias and complete-Hoeffding calibration term in a finite testing optimization, and pairs it with a separate finite mixture optimization over explicit bounded atomic amplitude laws whose second moment exactly matches the displayed rough-case repeated-observation coefficient. A common sharp rate is reported only after these objects are attained and matched.
